children: The civil aviation ministry has asked Adani Airports and airlines to work out a transition plan by 20 October after carriers opposed proposed changes to international operations at Terminal 2

The government has put Adani Airports’ proposed redevelopment of Mumbai airport’s Terminal 1 on hold after airlines opposed plans to reduce international flight operations at Terminal 2, with the Ministry of Civil Aviation giving stakeholders until 20 October to work out a transition plan.

The intervention follows Mumbai International Airport or MIAL proposal to cut 265 of the 770 weekly international departure slots at Terminal 2 from 26 October. The proposed reduction would affect 46 airlines, including IndiGo, which faces 74 slot cuts, Air India with 33, and Emirates and Etihad Airways with 10 each, according to media report.

MIAL has said the reduction is required to free up facilities at Terminal 2, including check-in counters, baggage belts, gates and office space, for domestic operations that would shift from Terminal 1 during its phased redevelopment. The move is intended to accommodate around five million additional passengers annually.
Airlines have opposed the proposed timeline, arguing that the changes would be difficult to implement operationally and require more time for planning.

The civil aviation ministry has asked Adani Airports, airlines and other stakeholders to reconvene and formulate an “agreeable” and “win-win” transition plan. It has also directed Adani Airports to submit its request for the Major Development Plan for the redevelopment of Terminal 1, a key requirement for taking the wider exercise forward.

Adani Airports has scheduled a fresh stakeholder meeting for 13 October. The ministry’s 20 October deadline gives airlines additional time to assess the operational requirements and formulate a coordinated response.

The issue is part of a wider restructuring of airport operations in Mumbai. Domestic traffic from Terminal 1 is planned to shift to Terminal 2, while some international services could eventually move to the new Navi Mumbai International Airport. The International Air Transport Association (IATA) has opposed any forced relocation of international services, arguing that transfers should be voluntary and based on consultation.
